verdicts.explanation: Both pages are role=product with a named single product, their own Product JSON-LD offer has an empty price field, and no price-shaped token appears anywhere in the raw HTML, so the page cannot state its own price to a non-rendering reader.

The homepage does carry an Organization JSON-LD block, but it declares only url, name and a return policy, with no sameAs array linking to any external profile, so an assistant still has nothing to disambiguate the brand from others of the same name.

This page is a category/listing hub for the keyboards line (filters for connectivity, platform and series, sort-by-price options), not a single product's page. It already carries CollectionPage and ItemList JSON-LD, which is what a listing hub owes; Product markup belongs on the individual product pages it links to, not on the hub itself.

fixes.quote: A stylish, compact keyboard and mouse combo
site_specific: Add the current price for POP Icon Combo as visible text in the page's server-rendered HTML, next to the product description, not only inside the client-side add-to-cart widget.
Set the price field of the existing Product/Offer JSON-LD block (currently empty) to the same value.
Repeat this for Keys-To-Go 2's product page, which has the same empty offer price.

fixes.quote: Introducing your new AI control center
site_specific: Add a sameAs array to the existing homepage Organization JSON-LD block (@id https://www.logitech.com/#organization), listing Logitech's official Wikipedia, Wikidata and primary social profile URLs.
Keep the same @id so the sameAs links attach to the organization already declared on the page.
